visual: Compact upright perennial with glossy, exceptionally dark burgundy-purple to near-black succulent foliage, topped by broad clusters of rich red flowers in late summer.
water: Water moderately while establishing, then sparingly; established plants are strongly drought tolerant.
soilWarning: Wet or rich soil brings rot
prune: Leave spent flower heads for winter structure if desired, then cut old stems to ground level as new growth begins in spring.
resilience: Highly drought tolerant once established and selected for strong disease resistance; good drainage remains essential in winter.
uses: Sunny border, gravel garden, rock garden, pollinator planting, cut flowers and containers.
uncertain: Black Knight is the trade designation; RHS records 'Dolseb' as the cultivar name.
RHS does not currently publish full cultivation data for this cultivar; H6 is supported by UK trade information describing hardiness to approximately −15°C.

visual: Strong upright perennial with fleshy rich-green foliage and large domed flower heads, opening from citron-green buds into soft coral-pink flowers in early autumn.
water: Water moderately while establishing; once established, water only during prolonged dry periods.
soilWarning: Wet or rich soil: flop and rot
prune: Leave dried flower heads through winter if desired, then remove old stems at ground level when fresh growth appears in spring.
resilience: Very cold hardy, drought tolerant and generally easy to grow; possible problems include aphids, mildew and crown or stem rots in unsuitable wet conditions.
uses: Sunny border, mass planting, gravel garden, wildlife garden, cut flowers, dried flowers and containers.
uncertain: The supplied label 'Coral Jade' is a recognised synonym; RHS accepts the cultivar spelling 'Coraljade'.
H7 is based on breeder hardiness down to USDA zone 3 rather than a published cultivar-specific RHS hardiness rating.

visual: Compact upright perennial with glossy foliage shifting through yellow-green, blue-green and purple into warm burgundy tones, topped by peach, coral and creamy flower clusters in late summer.
water: Low to moderate water needs; allow soil to dry between waterings once established.
soilWarning: Rich or wet soil loosens its habit
prune: Leave seed heads standing through winter for structure and wildlife, then cut old stems to ground level before new spring growth.
resilience: Very cold hardy, drought tolerant once established, deer resistant and strongly attractive to pollinators.
uses: Dry garden, sunny border, edging, mass planting, pollinator garden and containers.
uncertain: The supplied name 'Conga Lin' resolves confidently to Hylotelephium telephium 'Conga Line'.
Terra Nova lists USDA zones 4–9; H7 is a conservative UK-style interpretation of that cold tolerance rather than a cultivar-specific RHS rating.

visual: Compact aromatic evergreen shrub forming a rounded mound of narrow grey-green leaves with highly fragrant blue-purple flower spikes in summer.
water: Water regularly until established, then sparingly; mature plants are strongly drought tolerant.
soilWarning: Hates winter wet and rich feeding
prune: Deadhead and trim after flowering to maintain a compact shape. Avoid cutting deeply into old leafless wood, which may not regenerate.
resilience: Drought tolerant once established and highly attractive to pollinators; may occasionally be affected by rosemary beetle, froghoppers, grey mould or honey fungus.
uses: Path edging, herb garden, cottage garden, Mediterranean planting, gravel garden, wildlife garden and containers.
